text:
eli: Hi all, first-day question  I can see the cluster in kubectl but when I try `kubectl get pods -n teams/infra-tools` I get Forbidden. who should I ask for namespace access?

it-ops: welcome eli! :wave: Do you have an SSO-mapped k8s principal yet? run `kubectl config current-context` and share the email you used to sign up in DM.

eli: current-context is `redwood-gke-europe-west1`, signed up with eli@redwood.ai. I can list namespaces but not view pods in that namespace.

sarah: hey eli, i'm your eng buddy. for new hires we either 1) add you to the `devs-infra` AD group (longer-term) or 2) give an ephemeral ServiceAccount kubeconfig scoped to `teams/infra-tools` for the first week. which do you prefer?

eli: SA kubeconfig sounds simpler for now. I just need to inspect logs and port-forward a service to run locally.

it-ops: noted. creating SA `onboard-eli` in `teams/infra-tools`, Role with pods/pods/log and pods/portforward, and a RoleBinding. token expires in 7d. i'll attach kubeconfig to ticket ONB-499.

onboard-bot: Ticket ONB-499 created 4cc assignee: it-ops ETA: 1 hour.

it-ops: done. uploaded kubeconfig to the ticket and set context `onboard-eli-context` with namespace `teams/infra-tools`. steps logged in the runbook.

eli: confirmed, `kubectl get pods -n teams/infra-tools` works and `kubectl port-forward svc/debug-ui 8080:80 -n teams/infra-tools` forwarded fine. thanks!

sarah: welcome to the team, eli :tada: DM me if you need any app secrets or env files.
